stories.title: BTH Breaks Ground on 7-Building Port St. Lucie Warehouse Development
stories.excerpt: BTH Development Partners is moving ahead on Phase 1 of Tradition Commerce Park, a 530,000 square foot industrial park in Port St. Lucie. Miller Construction Company is building the project at 12051 SW Tom Mackie Boulevard. Claren Architecture and Planners is the architect., Tradition Commerce Park is master-planned industrial and flex development spanning about 34 acres. Developed by BTH Development Partners, Tradition Commerce Park is approved for seven industrial and flex buildings. Phase 1 encompasses vertical construction of Building 4 (approximately 28,800 square feet) and Building 5 (approximately 26,400 square feet). Both Phase 1 buildings features customizable tenant layouts, starting at 3,000 square feet, to meet the region’s surging demand for small- to mid-bay flex and light industrial space. Subsequent phases of Tradition Commerce Park are planned to deliver large-bay dock-high industrial distribution facilities of up to 166,968 square feet, as well as build-to-suit opportunities. Colliers International Florida serves as the exclusive leasing and sales brokerage for the development. The post BTH Breaks Ground on 7-Building Port St. Lucie Warehouse Development appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: BTH Development Partners breaks ground on 530K SF industrial park, Phase 1 in Port St. Lucie.
First two buildings (28.8K and 26.4K SF) feature customizable flex layouts starting 3K SF.
Subsequent phases planned for large-bay dock-high facilities up to 166.9K SF.
stories.summary: BTH Development Partners has started vertical construction on Phase 1 of Tradition Commerce Park, a 34-acre industrial/flex development in Port St. Lucie spanning 530,000 square feet across seven approved buildings. Phase 1 includes two flex buildings (55,200 SF combined) with customizable tenant spaces starting at 3,000 SF, responding to regional demand for small- to mid-bay space. Later phases will deliver large-bay dock-high distribution facilities.
stories.impact: Industrial supply does not directly affect multifamily, but the project signals robust logistics and e-commerce demand in Port St. Lucie, which may drive job growth, population inflow, and rental demand for workforce housing near the submarket. Monitor whether future residential development follows industrial absorption.

stories.title: Circle Realty Secures 38K SF of New Leases at 14 Penn Plaza
stories.excerpt: Circle Realty Group has closed on 37,600 square feet of new leases in Midtown, Commercial Observer has learned. The two largest deals at 225 West 34th Street, also known as 14 Penn Plaza, were for civil engineering company Bohler Engineering, which expanded from 8,000 square feet to 14,000 square feet, and cybersecurity firm T&M USA, which took 14,000 square feet, according to Circle Realty. Bohler signed a 10-year lease and asking rent in the building was $67 per square foot. The length of T&M’s lease was unclear. “These tenants came to me because we’re at the center of transportation and we have a first-class property,” Circle Realty President Jay Futersak told CO. “Tenants know that what we promised is what we deliver.” Futersak represented his own firm in-house and both tenants in the deals. Smaller recent deals in the building were for accounting and advisory firm Calibre CPA Group, which signed a 10-year, 6,100-square-foot lease and is relocating from 462 Seventh Avenue. Mark Furst and Benjamin Saftler of Kaufman Leasing, the brokerage arm of the Kaufman Organization, handled the deal for the Washington, D.C.-based accounting firm and did not immediately comment. Meanwhile, discrimination law firm Fitapelli & Schaffer is also relocating from 20 Liberty Street to 14 Penn with a new 3,514-square-foot lease. Robert Gallucci of Colliers negotiated on behalf of the law firm and did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Futersak repped ownership in-house in the Calibre and Fitapelli deals. Mark Hallum can be reached at mhallum@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Circle Realty closes 37.6K SF leases at 14 Penn Plaza (225 West 34th St), Midtown Manhattan.
Bohler Engineering expanded 8K to 14K SF (10-yr lease, $67/SF asking); T&M USA took 14K SF.
Tenants cite proximity to transit and first-class property quality as draw.
stories.summary: Circle Realty Group closed 37,600 square feet of new office leases at 14 Penn Plaza in Midtown Manhattan, with two anchor tenants: Bohler Engineering (civil engineering, expanded to 14,000 SF on 10-year lease at $67/SF) and cybersecurity firm T&M USA (14,000 SF). Smaller deals included Calibre CPA Group (6,100 SF, 10-year lease, relocating from nearby). Leasing agents cited the building's central transit location and quality as key tenant draw.
stories.impact: Midtown Manhattan office leasing strength is a weak signal for multifamily demand in the submarket—office growth typically precedes residential absorption lag in postwar CBDs. However, the consolidation of professional services and tech-adjacent tenants in transit-rich Midtown may increase demand for rentals among young professionals, particularly in nearby Hells Kitchen and Koreatown submarkets over 18–24 months.

stories.title: Sunday Summary: Who’s Funding $1.3 Trillion in Data Center Spending?
stories.excerpt: Pluck your average Commercial Observer journalist off the street, shove them in a van, shine a flashlight in their eyes, and say, “Quick — what’s the biggest story in commercial real estate?” nine reporters out of 10 will answer: “Data centers.” At least that’s the case in 2026 after the billions and billions of dollars in investment that have been lavished on the sector. Actually, make that trillion — with a “t.” It’s still a sector that’s largely mysterious and unknown (even the vocabulary of the asset class is new!) so CO was excited last week when San Diego-based Atrium, an AI analytics firm, launched an interactive data platform called “Who Finances America’s Data Centers,” which tracks the money behind the $1.3 trillion (and counting) data center bonanza. What makes Atrium’s platform so fascinating is that it delves into the nitty gritty of individual deals like Coreweave’s $23 billion debt facility from 38 different lenders, and the 24 lenders financing DigitalBridge and IFM’s $20 billion debt facility — but at the same time it examines the breadth of activity of non-bank lenders like PIMCO (which has done $23 billion in originations), or borrowers like Amazon, Microsoft, Google, Meta and Oracle (five firms that alone account for $223 billion in long-term debt and credit facilities). All this data center activity comes as construction costs have been on the rise. Construction might have slowed down in other sectors, but the explosive growth of data centers has seemingly made up for it, at least according to a recent report from Skanska. “The market is hot and cold right now — hot and warm may be a better way to say it — so what stands out is that we’re seeing a lot of project activity around data centers, semiconductor, life sciences,” said Skanska’s Tom Park. “There’s really a lot of unprecedented demand in the mechanical, electrical, plumbing and steel space driving up lead times and cost.” Moreover, the companies that rely on the proliferation of data cent
bullets: $1.3 trillion in data center investment tracked by new Atrium analytics platform.
CoreWeave secured $23B debt facility from 38 lenders; DigitalBridge/IFM closed $20B from 24 lenders.
PIMCO has originated $23B in data center lending; Amazon, Microsoft, Google, Meta, Oracle major borrowers.
stories.summary: Atrium, an AI analytics firm, launched an interactive platform tracking the $1.3 trillion (and growing) in data center investment and financing across the U.S. The platform reveals granular lending data, including CoreWeave's $23 billion debt facility (38 lenders), DigitalBridge/IFM's $20 billion facility (24 lenders), and PIMCO's $23 billion in originations. Major borrowers include Amazon, Microsoft, Google, Meta, and Oracle.
stories.impact: Massive data center capex creates indirect multifamily demand through job creation and wage growth in tech hubs (Northern California, Northern Virginia, Phoenix, Dallas). Developers should monitor data center deployment timelines and lender appetite in markets where cloud/AI compute infrastructure is expanding—expect 12–24 month lag before residential rental demand accelerates and construction costs rise in these hubs.

stories.title: Zimmet Law Group Signs 10-Year Lease for 515 Madison Ave.
stories.excerpt: GFP Real Estate announced that Zimmet Law Group P.C. has signed a new office lease for 5,476 square feet at 515 Madison Ave. in Manhattan’s Plaza District. Zimmet Law Group will occupy Suite 603 on the sixth floor of the building under a new 10-year lease, relocating its Manhattan office from 477 Madison Ave. The firm is expected to take occupancy following completion of its new space later this year. Martin McGrath and Kephra Stone of GFP Real Estate represented the landlord in-house. Elliot Zelinger of Savitt Partners represented Zimmet Law Group. “Zimmet Law Group’s decision to make a long-term commitment to 515 Madison Avenue speaks to the continued appeal of the building and the strength of the Plaza District,” said McGrath. “Professional services firms continue to prioritize high-quality, well-located office space, and we’re pleased to welcome Zimmet Law Group to the building.” The post Zimmet Law Group Signs 10-Year Lease for 515 Madison Ave. appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Zimmet Law Group signs 10-year lease for 5.5K SF at 515 Madison Ave, Manhattan Plaza District.
Relocating from 477 Madison Ave; taking occupancy later 2026.
Landlord rep cited professional services demand and building quality as lease driver.
stories.summary: GFP Real Estate announced that law firm Zimmet Law Group P.C. signed a new 10-year office lease for 5,476 square feet at 515 Madison Avenue in Manhattan's Plaza District, relocating from 477 Madison Avenue with occupancy expected later in 2026. Leasing brokers framed the deal as evidence of professional services firms' continued commitment to prime Manhattan office space.
stories.impact: Minimal impact on multifamily. A single professional services lease renewal within the same submarket suggests office market equilibrium in Plaza District but does not signal net job growth or population inflow material to apartment demand forecasts.

stories.title: Avison Young Recapitalization Provides “War Chest” for Further Growth
stories.excerpt: Avison Young’s newly announced recapitalization does more than deleverage the company’s balance sheet debt-to-EBITDA ratio to less than 3x, reduce debt and preferred equity by nearly 70% and give key financial partners a common equity position, although it accomplishes all of these. “We’re pretty excited,” Avison Young chair and CEO Mark E. Rose told Connect CRE. “This gives us the war chest to do the things that we’re known for”–namely, make strategic acquisitions, broaden the platform’s capabilities and expand the pool of talent through recruitment. “And we have our eyes on targets.” Expected to close in October, the new transaction builds upon the success of the company’s 2024 recapitalization. It also represents a rethinking of how to produce the best outcome for Avison Young’s longtime financial stakeholders as well as the company’s principals.   “It’s kind of simple,” said Rose. “Was it better to take the money and pay these [stakeholders], or was it better to invest and make them multiples of the same money? And after 16 months, that’s what we were able to come to.”  The process of devising this solution began in the spring of 2025, Rose said. The company looked at various options for taking the stakeholders’ investment and “putting it into a different form that would meet everybody’s needs.”  The solution entailed a 70% debt-to-equity swap, “giving us a debt-to-EBITDA ratio that’s under 3x so that we can build, effectively, a fund—a pool of capital along with additional new money that [the stakeholders] were putting in,” said Rose.  He continued, “What we needed to do was work with our financial stakeholders, convert them into equity holders.” Their ownership stake is
bullets: Avison Young recapitalization reduces debt/preferred equity 70%; debt-to-EBITDA below 3x.
Closing expected October 2026; builds on 2024 recapitalization.
CEO Mark Rose cites 'war chest' for acquisitions, platform expansion, and talent growth.
stories.summary: Avison Young announced a recapitalization that reduces debt and preferred equity by nearly 70% and lowers the company's debt-to-EBITDA ratio to below 3x. The transaction, expected to close in October 2026, follows the firm's 2024 recapitalization and provides capital for strategic acquisitions, capability expansion, and talent acquisition. CEO Mark Rose framed it as investing stakeholder proceeds to generate multiples over time.
stories.impact: No direct impact on multifamily supply or demand. However, improved capital structure at a major CRE brokerage/advisory platform may increase M&A activity and transaction velocity in the multifamily market, benefiting sellers and reducing financing friction for developers seeking acquisition finance or equity co-investment.

stories.title: Local Owner-Operator Snags Pico-Robertson Apartment Property
stories.excerpt: Marcus & Millichap closed the sale of 1476 S Shenandoah St., a 16-unit multifamily property in Los Angeles. The property sold for $5.3 million, or $334,937 per unit.  “Properties like this rarely become available in Pico-Robertson, especially those that have been held by the same ownership for more than two decades,” said Sam Liberow, senior managing director investments. “After 23 years of ownership, the offering generated six competitive offers, reflecting continued demand for well-located multifamily assets with large floor plans. The buyer plans to renovate units through natural tenant turnover while holding the property as a long-term investment.” Liberow, in Marcus & Millichap’s Encino office, marketed the property on behalf of the seller, 1476 Shenandoah Street LLC. He also procured the buyer, a local owner and operator. Built in 1966, the 17,653-square-foot property is situated on a 0.30-acre parcel in Los Angeles’ Pico-Robertson neighborhood. The conversations behind tomorrow’s apartment deals happen at Connect Apartments on September 22 in LA. Connect with the capital sources, owners, developers, and brokers driving multifamily investment. Learn more and reserve your seat at www.connectapts2026.com. The post Local Owner-Operator Snags Pico-Robertson Apartment Property appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Marcus & Millichap closes 16-unit sale in Pico-Robertson, Los Angeles for $5.3M ($334.9K/unit).
Property held by same owner 23 years; generated six competitive offers.
Buyer is local owner-operator; plans renovation via natural turnover and long-term hold.
stories.summary: Marcus & Millichap brokered the sale of 1476 South Shenandoah Street, a 16-unit apartment property in Los Angeles's Pico-Robertson neighborhood, for $5.3 million ($334,937 per unit). The 1966-built property on 0.30 acres was held by the original owner for 23 years and attracted six competitive offers, reflecting continued demand for vintage multifamily with large floor plans in well-located LA submarkets. The local owner-operator buyer plans unit renovations through natural tenant turnover.
stories.impact: Pico-Robertson is a vintage, supply-constrained submarket where redevelopment risk and entitlement friction limit new supply. Strong competition (six offers) and local buyer retention signals durable value in older walkable neighborhoods with good schools and proximity to West LA jobs. For developers: underwriting older small-building acquisitions for value-add renovation may outpace ground-up development in LA's tight neighborhoods; conversely, zoning changes permitting density in adjacent undersupplied pockets could unlock new supply.

stories.title: Grocery-Anchored Queens Retail Secures $32M Financing
stories.excerpt: Northmarq’s New York Metro Debt + Equity team, led by Robert Delitsky and Charles Cotsalas, arranged $32 million in financing for Springnex Plaza, a 96,028-square-foot retail property located in the Springfield Gardens neighborhood of Queens. Delitsky and Cotsalas arranged financing on behalf of the owner, Mattone Group Springnex LLC, through Principal Financial Group. “Ownership developed Springnex Plaza in 2000 and they have done a fabulous job maintaining very strong occupancy,” Delitsky said. “Supermarket-anchored shopping centers like Springnex Plaza will continue to attract very strong lender interest in today’s market,” added Cotsalas. Springnex Plaza is a 100% occupied, multi-tenant, grocery-anchored retail center situated on approximately 5.58 acres. Serving the Springfield Gardens community for more than two decades, Springnex Plaza offers a complementary mix of grocery, dining, healthcare and service-oriented tenants. Anchored by Stop & Shop, it’s home to a diverse roster of local and national retailers, including Ashley Stewart, IHOP and Northwell Health. The post Grocery-Anchored Queens Retail Secures $32M Financing appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Principal Financial Group closes $32M financing for Springnex Plaza, 96K SF grocery-anchored retail in Queens.
Property 100% occupied; anchored by Stop & Shop; developed 2000, maintained strong occupancy.
Lenders cite supermarket-anchored centers as attractive in current market.
stories.summary: Northmarq's New York debt team arranged $32 million in financing for Springnex Plaza, a fully occupied 96,028-square-foot grocery-anchored retail center in Springfield Gardens, Queens, developed in 2000. Anchored by Stop & Shop and occupied by tenants including IHOP, Ashley Stewart, and Northwell Health, the center sits on 5.58 acres. Principal Financial Group was the lender; brokers noted that supermarket-anchored shopping centers continue to attract strong lender interest.
stories.impact: Grocery-anchored retail financing strength in Queens suggests stable consumer fundamentals and demand for neighborhood shopping. However, minimal direct multifamily signal unless retail debt availability constrains multifamily capital competition. Monitor: if grocery chains expand into underserved Queens submarkets, adjacent residential development may follow; conversely, continued retail financing availability may indicate lender preference for retail over multifamily in outer boroughs, raising capital costs for apartment development.

stories.title: CoStar Closes $800M Cash Acquisition of New-Home Platform Zonda
stories.excerpt: CoStar Group, a leading provider of online real estate marketplaces, information, analytics and 3D digital twin technology, announced that it has completed its acquisition of Zonda, a new home-construction data, homebuilder software and residential real estate marketplace platform, for $800 million in cash. Zonda’s platform of proprietary lot-level construction and development data, which serves more than 3,000 homebuilders, developers, lenders and suppliers, gives CoStar a foothold in the $400 billion annual U.S. new-home sales market, according to the CoStar announcement. Based in Washington, D.C., Zonda generated approximately $170 million in revenue in 2025. CoStar’s acquisition of the platform was first announced in May. “Zonda has built an exceptional business around information the homebuilding industry relies on every day,” Andy Florance, founder and CEO of CoStar, said in announcing the deal’s closing. “This is a massive market with a sophisticated group of builders, developers, lenders, investors and suppliers that need purpose-built information, analytics and marketing solutions. With the acquisition now complete, we have the opportunity to bring together Zonda’s proprietary new construction data, software and builder relationships with CoStar Group’s technology, analytics and marketplace capabilities.” The deal provides Arlington, Va.-based CoStar with new-home data and analytics from Zonda, which tracks new-home communities, land development, construction activity, home sales and builder operations at the lot level. In addition, Zonda-owned residential marketplaces NewHomeSource.com and Livabl join CoStar’s portfolio, expanding its consumer marketplace business specifically into new construction. bullets: CoStar closes $800M cash acquisition of Zonda, new-home construction data and homebuilder platform.
Zonda serves 3K+ homebuilders, developers, lenders, suppliers; $170M 2025 revenue; $400B addressable market.
Acquisition provides CoStar foothold in new-home sales and lot-level construction data.
stories.summary: CoStar Group completed its $800 million cash acquisition of Zonda, a new-home construction data, homebuilder software, and residential real estate marketplace platform. Zonda serves more than 3,000 homebuilders, developers, lenders, and suppliers with proprietary lot-level construction and development data, generated approximately $170 million in 2025 revenue, and operates in the $400 billion annual U.S. new-home sales market. The acquisition, announced in May, extends CoStar's portfolio into single-family and residential development intelligence.
stories.impact: Significant indirect impact: CoStar's data aggregation and analytics strength now extends into homebuilder operations, lot acquisition, and supply-chain visibility. For multifamily developers, this may improve transparency into single-family supply/demand, labor/material costs, and regional construction bottlenecks—informing rental rate and underwriting assumptions. If CoStar integrates Zonda lot data with its apartment market intelligence, developers gain better tools to forecast rental demand in markets experiencing single-family sprawl vs. infill multifamily trends.

stories.title: Michael Troyanovsky of Regency Development Group: 5 Questions
stories.excerpt: With a population of less than 6,000, little Bay Harbor Islands, Fla., is often overlooked – but not by Regency Development Group. Since 2020, the developer has been building residential projects in the coastal community near Surfside, Indian Creek and Bal Harbour. Regency has four active projects on the island, including the 33-unit La Maré Regency, the nine-unit La Maré Signature and the 20-unit Bay Harbor Villas. Commercial Observer recently caught up with Michael Troyanovsky, managing partner and vice president of the family company, to discuss the submarket’s success. The following conversation has been edited for length and clarity.   Commercial Observer: Why Bay Harbor Islands? What caught your interest about that submarket? Michael Troyanovsky: A really valid question, because there were other hot spot areas that a lot of people were gravitating to when we first started buying Bay Harbor. We came to the area, and we really felt like it had the most potential. It was always overlooked. It’s honestly the most amazing hidden gem. It’s surrounded by the most beautiful waters, a little nook in the center of Miami. It’s getting more and more discovered. Since then, we really integrated into the island, and we really got to know the local community, the local governments, because we have to work very closely with them on getting all the projects approved and making sure that it fits the neighborhood and demographic. We opened up a big sales office here, and we plan to stay here for the future. Who are you finding is the target demographic for your units? It’s a little bit of a mix demographic-wise, but I would say a lot of people who, whether it’s local or international, really want boutique building living. bullets: Regency Development Group built four active residential projects in Bay Harbor Islands, Fla. since 2020.
Portfolio includes 33-unit La Maré Regency, 9-unit La Maré Signature, 20-unit Bay Harbor Villas.
Managing Partner Troyanovsky describes submarket as 'overlooked hidden gem' surrounded by waterfront.
stories.summary: Regency Development Group, a family developer, has concentrated four active residential projects in Bay Harbor Islands, Florida (population under 6,000) since 2020, including La Maré Regency (33 units), La Maré Signature (9 units), and Bay Harbor Villas (20 units). Managing Partner Michael Troyanovsky cited the coastal submarket's lack of competition, waterfront setting, and proximity to affluent neighbors (Surfside, Bal Harbour, Indian Creek) as draws overlooked by larger developers.
stories.impact: Bay Harbor Islands represents a niche, supply-constrained coastal submarket where a single local developer has de facto market power. This signals: (1) limited land availability and zoning constraints limiting new supply; (2) affluent demographics supporting premium rents; (3) potential for a consolidator to acquire aging inventory and convert or redevelop. For larger developers: small coastal Florida submarkets with reputation/zoning barriers may favor partnerships with local operators or selective infill development over large-scale new builds.

stories.title: JBL Asset Management Buys Retail Condo Near Miami Design District
stories.excerpt: Alta Developers sold off a retail condo near the Miami Design District for $17.3 million, property records show. JBL Asset Management purchased the 25,504-square-foot asset on the ground floor of the Quadro condo building. The property at 3900 Biscayne Boulevard faces train tracks, just east of the Miami Design District, an open-air, luxury mall. Quadro’s retail tenants include The Shade Store, 7th Avenue furniture store and Waterworks plumbing supply store. Hollywood, Fla.-based JBL is marketing a 2,358-square-foot suite as the last remaining retail space at the 407,498-square-foot condo building. Alta Developers completed the 200-unit building in 2019. The purchase comes as the 18-block Design District, one of the country’s highest-grossing upscale malls, is undergoing a major expansion. Earlier this week, its owners, entities tied to Miami-based Craig Robins and LVMH billionaire Bernard Arnault, scored a $125 million construction loan to build a Snøhetta-designed, mixed-use building. The joint venture also launched sales for Fouquet’s condo and hotel development, designed by Pritzker Prize winner David Chipperfield. Representatives for Alta Developers and JBL Asset Management did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Julia Echikson can be reached at jechikson@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: JBL Asset Management purchases 25.5K SF retail condo near Miami Design District for $17.3M.
Ground floor of Quadro building; tenants: The Shade Store, 7th Avenue, Waterworks.
Design District undergoing major expansion; owners securing $125M construction loan for mixed-use building.
stories.summary: JBL Asset Management acquired a 25,504-square-foot ground-floor retail condo in the Quadro building near the Miami Design District for $17.3 million from Alta Developers. Tenants include The Shade Store, 7th Avenue furniture, and Waterworks plumbing supply; one 2,358-SF suite remains available. The acquisition coincides with Design District owners (entities tied to Craig Robins and LVMH's Bernard Arnault) securing a $125 million construction loan for a Snøhetta-designed mixed-use building and launching Fouquet's condo and hotel sales.
stories.impact: Design District expansion and mixed-use repositioning will likely drive residential demand through retail/hospitality job creation and lifestyle amenity clustering. The $125M construction loan signals strong capital appetite for Miami luxury mixed-use development. Developers should monitor Design District housing components and timing—they may cannibalize demand in adjacent Wynwood, Buena Vista, and Allapattah multifamily markets, or conversely, create spill-over demand if Design District residential units sell/lease ahead of supply. Monitor Fouquet's hotel/condo absorption rates as leading indicator of Miami luxury residential appetite.
